entries.description: Validate a structured invoice JSON object for EU compliance: checks required/recommended fields, line-item and tax math, and returns errors/warnings plus an eu_compliant verdict.

FIELD-NAME TRAPS confirmed live: amounts must use `tax_amount` (NOT `tax`) and each line_item must include `line_total` (NOT `amount`) — otherwise the engine reports subtotal/total mismatches and skips line-item math (line_items_check stays 0).

Required invoice fields: invoice_number, invoice_date, vendor_vat, vendor_name, vendor_address, line_items, amounts. Recommended (warning-only): buyer_name, buyer_vat, buyer_address, due_date, currency.

Most expensive op in the bundle at $0.54/call.
Unknown fields come back null; confidence object grades vendor_name/total_amount/line_items/vat_amount as high/low.

entries.name: Tax Calculator
entries.description: General tax/sales-tax calculation from amount and jurisdiction inputs. Pay-per-call x402.

usage.outputShape: body.estimated_tax (number), body.breakdown.federal, body.breakdown.state, body.tips[] (string array of advice), body.processedAt
quirks: inputSchema is null in the registry; the REAL required fields are income (number) and location (string) — NOT amount/state/zip. Sending amount/state/zip returns HTTP 400 (but you are still charged $0.01).
Despite the name 'Tax Calculator' and subcat 'tax-compliance', this is an INCOME tax estimator (returns federal + state income tax + savings tips), not a sales-tax calculator.
location accepts a state name like 'California'.
qa-pay reported confirmed:false and txHash:null but status 200 + paid true; settlement not surfaced in response.
usage.guide: POST to https://gg402.vercel.app/tax_calc with a JSON body containing income (a number, e.g. annual income) and location (a string, e.g. a US state name like 'California'). It is a paid x402 endpoint costing $0.01 USDC on Base, no auth/SIWX needed. The response is synchronous JSON: read body.estimated_tax for the total estimated income tax, body.breakdown.federal and body.breakdown.state for the split, and body.tips[] for tax-saving suggestions. Do not send amount/state/zip — those wrong field names return a 400 yet still charge you.

entries.name: OpenSanctions Screening
entries.description: Screen people/entities against global sanctions, PEP and watchlists for compliance/KYC. Pay-per-call x402.

usage.outputShape: body.sanctioned (bool), body.matchCount (number), body.matches[] with .caption, .entityType, .topics[], .matchedOn[], .datasets[], .countries[]
quirks: All inputs are URL query params, not a JSON body (it is a GET).
Only name is required; country/address/birthDate are optional filters that cut false positives.
sanctioned:false with empty matches[] means clean — that is a valid successful result, not an error.
Common names without country/birthDate can return multiple matches; inspect matchedOn per entry for confidence (name is always present, country/birthDate indicate stronger hits).
usage.guide: Call GET https://scan.madhousewallet.com/api/public/sanctions-check with the entity name as the required `name` query param (URL-encode spaces); optionally add country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), address, and birthDate to reduce false positives. Pay $0.04 USDC via x402 on Base (also accepts Polygon/Arbitrum). Read body.sanctioned for the boolean verdict and body.matches[] for matched entities — each match has caption, entityType, topics (sanction/role.pep/etc.), matchedOn, and source datasets. sanctioned:false with empty matches means the entity is clean.

entries.name: MiCA Compliance Pre-flight
entries.description: EU stablecoin MiCA compliance pre-flight check for tokens/services. Pay-per-call x402.

usage.callShape: POST https://tooloracle.io/v2/compliance_preflight with JSON body {token, issuer, jurisdiction}
usage.outputShape: JSON-RPC envelope. Parse the JSON string at body.result.content[0].text, then read: data.decision (e.g. "PASS"), data.reason_codes[] (e.g. ["ALL_CHECKS_PASSED"]), data.evidence.mica.verdict, data.evidence.custody. Signed attestation at body.result._meta.grounding_receipt.
quirks: Response is a JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope (jsonrpc/id/result), not a flat JSON object.
The actual compliance result is a JSON STRING nested at result.content[0].text and must be JSON.parse'd a second time.
result._meta.grounding_receipt carries a cryptographically signed attestation (ES256K + ML-DSA-65 PQC, NIST beacon anchors) over the input/output hashes.
Backend is an MCP server (server_did did:web:feedoracle.io) fronted at tooloracle.io; observed_auth_method=anonymous despite x402 payment.
x402 paid $0.01 on Base; qa-pay reported confirmed:false / txHash:null but call returned 200 with real data.
usage.guide: POST to https://tooloracle.io/v2/compliance_preflight with a JSON body describing the token/service to check, e.g. {"token":"USDC","issuer":"Circle","jurisdiction":"EU"}. Pay $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base (no API key, no sign-in). The response is a JSON-RPC envelope: parse the JSON string at result.content[0].text, then read data.decision (PASS/FAIL), data.reason_codes[], and data.evidence (mica verdict, custody risk, etc.). A signed grounding receipt sits at result._meta.grounding_receipt if you need attestation.

entries.name: Greeneris EU EORI Validation
entries.description: Validate an EU EORI (Economic Operators Registration and Identification) customs number live against the official European Commission EOS/DDS2 registry, returning valid true/false plus the registered operator name and address when the operator consented to publication.

queryParams.eori: REQUIRED. EORI number: 2-letter country code + 1-15 alphanumerics (FR uses SIRET), e.g. FR38347481400100

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/eu/eori?eori=<EORI_NUMBER> (2-letter country code + 1-15 alphanumerics). x402 paid endpoint (~0.003 USDC on Base, no API key) — pay the 402 quote and re-request.
usage.outputShape: JSON: { ok: true, data: { eori, valid (bool), name, address, status_description, source } }. name/address are populated only when the operator consented to publication in the EU registry.
quirks: Single required query param: eori (2-letter country code + 1-15 alphanumerics; France uses the SIRET-based form, e.g. FR38347481400100 = AIRBUS).
Backed by the European Commission EOS/DDS2 SOAP service; returned as clean JSON. Results are 24h cached.
name and address are only returned when the operator consented to publication — an EORI can be valid:true with no name/address.
Static price ($0.003), not a dynamic quote (accepts amount 3000 = 0.003 USDC, 6 decimals).
Distinct from Greeneris EU Company Check, which carries EORI only as one optional sub-check; this endpoint is a dedicated single-purpose EORI validator.
Part of Greeneris 'eu-verify' — sibling validators (/v1/eu/vat-check, /v1/validate/*, /v1/eu/company-check, /v1/global/lei) live on the same host as separate services.
usage.guide: Validate an EU customs EORI number against the official European Commission registry. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/eu/eori?eori=<EORI> where EORI is a 2-letter country code followed by 1-15 alphanumerics (France uses the SIRET-based form, e.g. FR38347481400100 for AIRBUS). It is an x402 paid endpoint (~0.003 USDC on Base, no API key) — pay the 402 quote and re-request. Read data.valid (bool); when the operator consented to publication you also get data.name and data.address. Use for customs/KYB checks before trading with an EU business.

entries.name: Greeneris French Invoice-Ready Check
entries.description: One-call French e-invoicing compliance check by SIREN or SIRET — runs the Luhn checksum, confirms existence and active status in the official SIRENE registry, computes the FR VAT number and validates it live against VIES, returning a single ready / not_ready / check_vat_manually verdict. Keyless over x402. $0.02.

siret.description: 14-digit SIRET; the SIREN is extracted from it (this or siren is required)

outputSchema.description: { ok, data: { siren, checksum_valid, exists, active, legal_name, vat_number, vat_status, invoice_ready, verdict, details, source } }

usage.outputShape: JSON: { ok:true, data:{ siren, checksum_valid:bool, exists:bool, active:bool, legal_name, vat_number, vat_status, invoice_ready:bool, verdict:'ready'|'not_ready'|'check_vat_manually', details, source } }
quirks: Exactly one of siren (9 digits) or siret (14 digits) is required; passing a SIRET extracts the SIREN from it.
verdict is one of ready / not_ready / check_vat_manually — the last is returned when VIES is unreachable, so VIES flakiness never blocks the answer (invoice_ready then reflects checksum+SIRENE only).
Built for the French e-invoicing reform: from 2026-09-01 the customer's SIREN is a mandatory invoice mention. Returns firmographic legal_name only, no people (GDPR).
Data sources: recherche-entreprises.api.gouv.fr (INSEE SIRENE) + VIES REST API (European Commission); the Luhn checksum and FR VAT key are computed locally. Responses are 1h cached.
Only French entities are covered — this host has sibling per-country company/registry endpoints but no invoice-ready equivalent for other countries.
usage.guide: French e-invoicing readiness check for KYB / invoice compliance. Pass ?siren= a 9-digit SIREN (or ?siret= a 14-digit SIRET) of the customer you're about to invoice. Read data.verdict ('ready' | 'not_ready' | 'check_vat_manually') plus the component flags checksum_valid / exists / active / vat_status and the computed vat_number (e.g. FR27552032534). Use invoice_ready as the boolean gate. No API key — pay the x402 402 (Base USDC, $0.02). For generic (non-FR) VAT validation use the Strale EU VAT Validate entry instead.

entries.name: Greeneris SIRET Validation
entries.description: Offline checksum validation of French company numbers: auto-detects SIREN (9 digits) vs SIRET (14 digits) and applies the INSEE Luhn rule plus the documented La Poste exception, returning validity, type, siren and nic.

number.description: SIREN (9 digits) or SIRET (14 digits); spaces/dots/dashes tolerated, passed as the ?number= query param

usage.outputShape: ok (bool), data.{number, valid (bool), type (siren|siret), rule (e.g. luhn), siren, nic, source}
quirks: number is a REQUIRED query param; separators (spaces/dots/dashes) are tolerated and stripped.
Auto-detects SIREN (9 digits) vs SIRET (14 digits) and reports it in data.type.

Pure OFFLINE checksum computation (INSEE Luhn + La Poste 356000000* exception) — it does NOT confirm the company exists in any registry; use /v1/fr/company or /v1/fr/invoice-ready for a registry lookup.
Response is 1y-cached; the provider does not charge for empty/failed answers.
Static price ($0.001); not a dynamic quote.
usage.guide: Validate a French SIREN or SIRET number's checksum offline before invoicing or before a costly Sirene registry call. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/fr/siret-check?number=<SIREN_OR_SIRET> (separators tolerated). Output: ok (bool) + data.{number, valid, type (siren|siret), rule, siren, nic, source}. Offline INSEE Luhn + La Poste exception only — checksum validity, not registry existence.

entries.name: Stratalize Regulatory Comment Deadlines
entries.description: Attested tracker of US Federal Register proposed rules and notices with open public-comment periods — returns upcoming comment-close deadlines (filtered client-side on comments_close_on over a days-ahead horizon, with optional search term and agency filters) pulled live from the Federal Register API.

days_ahead.description: Horizon in days ahead to include comment windows closing on/before (default returns near-term). Example: 1.

term.description: Optional full-text search term to filter Federal Register documents (e.g. "artificial intelligence").

agencies.description: Optional list of agency slugs to filter by.

items.description: Federal Register document with an open comment period (title, agencies, document_number, comments_close_on, html_url, etc.)

usage.callShape: POST https://www.stratalize.com/api/x402/regulatory-comment-deadlines with JSON body {"days_ahead":1} (optional term string, optional agencies[]). x402 USDC on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana; no API key, no account. NOTE: despite the 402 challenge labeling method GET, execution requires POST.
usage.outputShape: JSON with tool ('get_regulatory_comment_deadlines'), open_comment_count, days_ahead (echoed), filter_note (explains client-side comments_close_on filtering), documents[] (Federal Register documents with an open comment period), data_source ('Federal Register API (client-side comment window filter)'), freshness ('live'), retrieved_at, synthesis_id, plus an attested settlement receipt envelope (_stratalize with ML-DSA-65 signature + verify URL; receipt_id, verified_at trust.stratalize.com/verify; _receipt with payment.settlement_tx_hash + chain + amount_atomic and post-quantum signature). Observed on a verified 200 for {days_ahead:1}: open_comment_count 0, documents[] empty (no comment window closes within a 1-day horizon), settlement_tx_hash 0x555b7d92b979288f5afa06fd2ee1a7ac7ee2867b2f4b5f64585391f2d175e48d on Base.
quirks: Execution is POST with a JSON body, NOT GET — the x402 402 challenge and its bazaar extensions.info.input.method both mislabel the method as GET; per sibling Stratalize ops a paid GET returns HTTP 405 'Use POST to execute paid tool calls'.

days_ahead is the primary filter (integer, minimum 1); term and agencies are optional. A small days_ahead (e.g. 1) can legitimately return open_comment_count 0 with an empty documents[] when no comment window closes within that horizon — use a larger days_ahead to see upcoming deadlines.
Comment windows are filtered CLIENT-SIDE on comments_close_on (per filter_note) because the Federal Register API does not guarantee server-side open-window filtering.
Host stratalize.com 308-redirects to www.stratalize.com; call the canonical www host.
Every response carries a cryptographically signed post-quantum (ML-DSA-65) settlement receipt (receipt_id + settlement_tx_hash + verify URL at trust.stratalize.com/verify).
Fixed price $0.10 (amount 100000, USDC 6 decimals); not dynamic. Payable in USDC on Base or Solana, no API key.
usage.guide: Attested tracking of US Federal Register proposed rules and notices with OPEN public-comment periods — for compliance, government-affairs, and policy-monitoring agents that need upcoming comment-submission deadlines. Call POST https://www.stratalize.com/api/x402/regulatory-comment-deadlines with a JSON body {"days_ahead":30} (optionally a search term and/or an agencies[] filter); use a larger days_ahead to widen the horizon (a small value can return zero results). Pay per call via x402 USDC on Base or Solana — no API key or account. Returns Federal Register documents whose comment windows close within the horizon (filtered client-side on comments_close_on), sourced live from the Federal Register API, plus a cryptographically attested settlement receipt verifiable at trust.stratalize.com/verify. IMPORTANT: use POST, not GET — the x402 challenge mislabels the method and a GET returns 405.

entries.name: Agentstools Tax Brackets
entries.description: US federal tax reference tables for a year and filing status: the ordered income-tax brackets, standard deduction, long-term capital-gains breakpoints, FICA/self-employment constants, and the net investment income tax threshold (IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 + SSA 2026). Pure lookup, not tax advice.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/tax/brackets?filing_status=<status>&tax_year=<year> (both query params OPTIONAL; default filing_status=single, tax_year=2026). No body. x402 v2 on Base USDC, $0.002. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous).
usage.outputShape: filing_status (string echo), tax_year (int), standard_deduction (number USD), brackets (array of {rate, from, to} — to is null on the top bracket), capital_gains_longterm ({rate_0_up_to, rate_15_up_to, rate_20_above}), fica_constants ({oasdi_rate, oasdi_wage_base, medicare_rate, additional_medicare_rate, additional_medicare_threshold, se_oasdi_rate, se_medicare_rate, se_net_factor}), niit ({rate, threshold}), source (citation string), disclaimer
quirks: Both params are OPTIONAL query params on a GET (no body); omitting them defaults to filing_status=single, tax_year=2026
filing_status is an enum: single | married_jointly | married_separately | head_of_household
The top income bracket has "to": null (open-ended); rates are decimals (0.1 = 10%)
Reference data only — sourced from IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 + SSA 2026; the body carries a 'not tax advice' disclaimer
This is a pure lookup/dump; it does not compute a tax owed — use /tax/income or /tax/paycheck for calculations
usage.guide: US federal tax reference tables for a year and filing status. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/tax/brackets?filing_status=<single|married_jointly|married_separately|head_of_household>&tax_year=<year> — both query params are OPTIONAL (default single/2026). No body. x402 v2 on Base USDC, $0.002. Synchronous — the 200 body returns {filing_status, tax_year, standard_deduction, brackets[{rate,from,to}], capital_gains_longterm, fica_constants, niit, source, disclaimer}. Pure lookup (IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 + SSA 2026), not tax advice.

entries.name: Agentstools Capital Gains Tax
entries.description: Estimates US federal capital-gains tax on a gain — long-term 0/15/20 percent rates or short-term ordinary rates, plus the 3.8 percent net investment income tax (NIIT) — stacked on top of ordinary income. Pure local computation over IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 breakpoints; a reference estimate, not tax advice.

holding_period.description: long uses 0/15/20 rates; short uses ordinary rates. Default long behaviour per example.

ordinary_income.description: Other taxable income, used to stack the gain into brackets.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/tax/capgains?gain=<AMOUNT>&holding_period=<long|short>&ordinary_income=<AMOUNT>&filing_status=<single|married_jointly|married_separately|head_of_household>&tax_year=<YEAR> — all query params, no body. Only gain is required; the rest have defaults (filing_status=single, tax_year=2026). x402 v2 on Base USDC, $0.003. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous).
usage.outputShape: filing_status, holding_period, gain, ordinary_income (echoed) · cap_gains_rate (blended effective LT rate) · cap_gains_tax (number, USD) · cap_gains_breakdown[] ({rate, amount_in_bracket, tax} per 0/15/20 bracket layer) · niit (number, NIIT owed) · niit_rate (0.038) · niit_threshold (filing-status MAGI threshold) · total (number, cap_gains_tax + niit) · tax_year (int) · source (citation string) · disclaimer
quirks: gain is the only REQUIRED query param; holding_period/ordinary_income/filing_status/tax_year are optional with defaults (filing_status=single, tax_year=2026).
All inputs are QUERY params on a GET (no request body); despite the JSON-looking documented example, values go in the query string.
Pure local computation — not tax advice; breakpoints from IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (2026 tax year). Response carries a disclaimer field.

holding_period=long uses the layered 0/15/20 percent long-term rates (see cap_gains_breakdown[]); holding_period=short taxes the gain at ordinary rates as the incremental tax of stacking it on ordinary_income.
NIIT (3.8 percent) is added on the lesser of the gain and income above the filing-status threshold; niit=0 when below threshold.
usage.guide: Estimate US federal capital-gains tax. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/tax/capgains with query params: gain (REQUIRED, >=0), holding_period (long|short, long uses 0/15/20 rates), ordinary_income (stacks the gain into brackets), filing_status (single|married_jointly|married_separately|head_of_household, default single), tax_year (default 2026). No body. x402 v2 on Base USDC, $0.003. Synchronous — the 200 body carries {cap_gains_rate, cap_gains_tax, cap_gains_breakdown[], niit, niit_rate, niit_threshold, total, tax_year, source, disclaimer}. Pure computation over IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32; a reference estimate, not tax advice.

entries.name: Agentstools FICA Tax Estimate
entries.description: Estimates US FICA payroll taxes from annual wages — Social Security (OASDI), Medicare, and the additional Medicare surtax for employees, or self-employment tax (both halves plus the deductible half) when self_employed is set.

wages.description: Annual wages or net self-employment earnings (>= 0). Required.

self_employed.description: True computes self-employment tax (both halves + deductible half); default false

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/tax/fica with query params: wages (required, number >= 0), filing_status (optional enum: single|married_jointly|married_separately|head_of_household, default single), self_employed (optional boolean, default false), tax_year (optional integer, default 2026). No request body. Pays $0.003 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Result returned inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: self_employed (bool); wages; filing_status; social_security; medicare; additional_medicare; additional_medicare_threshold; oasdi_wage_base; total; tax_year; source (citations: IRS Rev. Proc./SSA base/Tax Foundation); disclaimer.
quirks: The 402 quote is delivered in the 'payment-required' response HEADER (base64 x402 v2 envelope); the 402 body is an empty '{}'. Wallets that read accepts only from the JSON body will fail to pay — read the header.
All inputs are query params; wages is the only required one. There is no request body (documented methods are GET/HEAD/DELETE).
Pure local computation using SSA 2026 wage base and IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 thresholds; a reference estimate, explicitly not tax advice (disclaimer field).
For self_employed=true the calc applies both OASDI+Medicare halves to 92.35% of net earnings plus the additional Medicare surtax and the deductible half of SE tax.
usage.guide: Estimate US FICA/payroll taxes in one paid call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/tax/fica?wages=<annual_wages> with optional filing_status (single|married_jointly|married_separately|head_of_household), self_employed (true|false), and tax_year. Pays $0.003 USDC via x402 on Base. Returns social_security, medicare, additional_medicare (with its threshold), the oasdi_wage_base, and the total, plus tax_year, source citations and a not-tax-advice disclaimer. Verified live: wages=200000, single, employee -> social_security 11439, medicare 2900, additional_medicare 0, total 14339, oasdi_wage_base 184500, tax_year 2026.

entries.name: Agentstools Paycheck Estimate
entries.description: US take-home paycheck estimate — federal income tax plus payroll (FICA) tax and an optional flat state estimate, returning total tax, effective rate, net pay per year and per pay period, and disposable income.

pay_period.description: Pay period for the per-period figures, default annual.

state.description: Optional two-letter US state code (adds a flat state-tax estimate).

pretax_deductions.description: Annual pretax deductions such as 401k, default 0. Reduces the income-tax base but not payroll wages.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/tax/paycheck with query params (required: gross_income; optional: filing_status, pay_period, state, pretax_deductions, tax_year). No body. x402 v2 on Base USDC, $0.008. Result inline in the 200 body (synchronous).
usage.outputShape: Object with taxable_income, federal_income_tax, fica{social_security, medicare, additional_medicare, total}, total_tax, total_effective_rate (fraction), net_pay_annual, net_pay_per_period, gross_per_period, disposable_income, periods_per_year, plus state/state_name/state_rate/state_tax when a state code is given, tax_year, source (citations), and a disclaimer.
quirks: gross_income is the only REQUIRED param; all others default (filing_status=single, pay_period=annual, pretax_deductions=0, tax_year=2026)
All inputs are QUERY params on a GET — there is no request body
state is optional; passing a two-letter code (e.g. CO) adds a FLAT state-tax estimate (state_rate/state_tax) — it does not model progressive state brackets
pretax_deductions reduce the federal income-tax base but NOT payroll (FICA) wages, so Social Security/Medicare are still computed on gross
total_effective_rate is a fraction (e.g. 0.245116 = 24.51%), not a percentage
Composite endpoint: reuses the /tax/income and /tax/fica math internally
Pure reference computation, explicitly not tax advice (see disclaimer field)
usage.guide: US take-home paycheck estimator. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/tax/paycheck with query params: gross_income (required, annual USD), filing_status (single|married_jointly|married_separately|head_of_household, default single), pay_period (annual|monthly|semimonthly|biweekly|weekly, default annual), state (optional two-letter code adds a flat state-tax estimate), pretax_deductions (annual 401k-style, default 0), tax_year (default 2026). No body. x402 v2 on Base USDC, $0.008, synchronous. The 200 body returns federal income tax, FICA (Social Security + Medicare), optional state tax, total tax, effective rate, and net/disposable pay per year and per period. Reference estimate only, not tax advice.

entries.name: Agentstools Insurance Model Law
entries.description: Turns a NAIC insurance model law (by model number or title keyword) into a normalized, machine-readable state-by-state adoption tracker across all 50 states, DC and US territories — each jurisdiction classified as MODEL_ADOPTION, PREVIOUS_VERSION, RELATED_ACTIVITY or NO_CURRENT_ACTIVITY with its statutory citation, plus NAIC provenance/attribution. Cited adoption facts only; the copyrighted NAIC model text is never rehosted.

model.description: NAIC model number such as 22, or a title keyword such as 'annuity suitability'.

adoption.description: Keyed by US jurisdiction name; each value is {classification, citation|null, columns|null, note|null}.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/insurance/model-law?model=<number-or-keyword>. One query param `model` (aliases: `number` for the integer, `keyword` for a title term). No body. x402 v2 on Base USDC, $0.03. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous).
usage.outputShape: found (bool), query (echo of {model}), model ({number, title, model_text_url}), adoption (object keyed by jurisdiction name → {classification: MODEL_ADOPTION|PREVIOUS_VERSION|RELATED_ACTIVITY|NO_CURRENT_ACTIVITY, citation|null, columns|null, note|null}) covering 50 states + DC + territories, summary ({states_total, by_classification counts}), provenance ({source_url, naic_version, retrieved}), linkback (NAIC PDF url), sources ({errors, partial, used[]}), attribution (string[]), disclaimer (not-legal-advice string).
quirks: Supply `model` as either a NAIC model number (e.g. 22, 170=Long-Term Care Insurance, 880=Insurance Data Security, 895=Annuity Suitability) OR a title keyword the route resolves to a model; `number` and `keyword` are documented aliases
Classifications are the NAIC Legal Division's own scheme; NO_CURRENT_ACTIVITY / RELATED_ACTIVITY jurisdictions carry a null citation, adopted ones carry the exact statutory citation
summary.states_total counted 56 in the probed response (50 states + DC + 5 territories)
Cited adoption facts only — the copyrighted NAIC model text and compiled chart pages are NOT rehosted; the body carries mandatory NAIC attribution and a 'not legal advice' disclaimer
Hard-cached: the NAIC charts change roughly once every year or two (probed response was NAIC 'Fall 2025')
usage.guide: Per-state adoption tracker for a NAIC insurance model law. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/insurance/model-law?model=<number-or-keyword> — pass a NAIC model number (e.g. 22) or a title keyword (e.g. 'annuity suitability'); `number`/`keyword` are aliases for `model`. No body. x402 v2 on Base USDC, $0.03, synchronous. The 200 body returns {found, model{number,title}, adoption{<jurisdiction>:{classification,citation}}, summary{states_total,by_classification}, provenance, linkback, attribution, disclaimer}. Classification enum: MODEL_ADOPTION, PREVIOUS_VERSION, RELATED_ACTIVITY, NO_CURRENT_ACTIVITY. Reference/compliance data (normalized NAIC facts with linkback), not legal advice.

entries.name: Agentstools Insurance State Adoption
entries.description: Returns which NAIC insurance model laws a given US state has adopted, inverted from the NAIC state-page corpus, with each model's adoption classification, statutory citation and a linkback to the NAIC source PDF.

state.description: US state or territory name or 2-letter code, such as California or CA.

model.description: Optional NAIC model number(s) to check, comma separated.

topic.description: Optional keyword to filter the models scanned (e.g. annuity).

adopted.description: Models the state has adopted; each {number, title, classification, citation, linkback}.

scanned.description: Every model scanned with its resolution status; each {number, title, status}.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/insurance/state-adoption with QUERY params (no body): state (US name or 2-letter code) plus optional model (NAIC model number(s), comma separated) and/or topic (keyword filter). Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.03 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: found (bool), state, adopted[] where each item is {number, title, classification (e.g. MODEL_ADOPTION / RELATED_ACTIVITY), citation (statutory cite), linkback (NAIC source PDF URL)}, summary {models_scanned, adopted_count, coverage, scan_cap, note}, scanned[] {number, title, status (ok/no_chart)}, provenance {source, retrieved}, sources {errors, partial, used}, attribution[], disclaimer. Verified live for {state:'New York', topic:'annuity'} -> found:true, 3 adopted annuity models: #245 Annuity Disclosure Model Regulation (RELATED_ACTIVITY, N.Y. COMP. CODES R. & REGS. tit. 11 §§40.0-40.6), #250 Variable Annuity Model Regulation, #821 Model Rule for a New Annuity Mortality Table (MODEL_ADOPTION); summary models_scanned 6, adopted_count 3, coverage bounded_default, scan_cap 8; each with a content.naic.org linkback PDF.
quirks: Params go in the QUERY STRING, not a body — this is a GET.

Without a model/topic filter the scan is BOUNDED (coverage 'bounded_default', scan_cap 8) — it scans only a subset of the NAIC model corpus. Pass model= (NAIC number(s), comma separated) or topic= to target specific models for full coverage.
state accepts either the full name ('New York') or the 2-letter code ('NY').
classification is the NAIC Legal Division's interpretation (MODEL_ADOPTION, RELATED_ACTIVITY, etc.) and may differ from the state's own view.
Each adopted model carries a statutory citation and a linkback to the NAIC source PDF; NAIC model text and compiled chart pages are NOT rehosted, only the adoption fact + citation.
scanned[] lists every model examined and its status ('ok' or 'no_chart' when NAIC has no state chart for that model).
Attribution (NAIC / content.naic.org, © NAIC) and the not-legal-advice disclaimer are returned and should be displayed.
Distinct from the sibling /insurance/model-law (single model law detail) and /insurance/bulletins.
usage.guide: Find out which NAIC insurance model laws a US state has adopted in one keyless x402 call, instead of manually reading NAIC state-page charts. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/insurance/state-adoption with QUERY params: state (full name or 2-letter code) plus an optional model= (NAIC model number(s), comma separated) and/or topic= keyword to narrow the scan. Synchronous — the 200 body carries adopted[] (each model's number, title, adoption classification, statutory citation, and NAIC linkback PDF), a summary (models_scanned, adopted_count, coverage, scan_cap), scanned[] with per-model resolution status, provenance/attribution, and a not-legal-advice disclaimer. NOTE: with no model/topic filter the scan is bounded to a subset of the corpus (coverage 'bounded_default') — pass model or topic for full coverage of the models you care about. Pays $0.03 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453). Example: {state:'New York', topic:'annuity'} -> 3 adopted annuity models incl. #245 Annuity Disclosure and #821 the new annuity mortality-table rule.

entries.name: Greeneris EU VAT Validation
entries.description: Validate an intra-EU VAT number live against the European Commission VIES REST API, returning is_valid plus the registered trader name and address (when the member state publishes them) and a compliance request_date timestamp.

queryParams.cc: REQUIRED. EU member state code (2 letters, incl. EL for Greece and XI for Northern Ireland), e.g. IE, FR, EL, XI
queryParams.vat: REQUIRED. VAT number WITHOUT the country prefix, e.g. 6388047V

data.name: string (registered trader name, when the member state publishes it)
data.source: string ('VIES REST API (European Commission, DG TAXUD) ...')

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/eu/vat-check?cc=<MEMBER_STATE_CODE>&vat=<VAT_NUMBER_NO_PREFIX>. x402 paid endpoint (~0.005 USDC on Base, no API key) — pay the 402 quote and re-request.
usage.outputShape: JSON: { ok: true, data: { country_code, vat_number, is_valid (bool), name, address, request_date (ISO), user_error, source } }. name/address are populated only when the member state publishes them; is_valid is the boolean gate.
quirks: Two required query params: cc (2-letter EU member state code — use EL for Greece and XI for Northern Ireland, not GR/GB) and vat (the VAT number WITHOUT its country prefix).
Backed by the live European Commission VIES REST API (DG TAXUD) — real-time query of the member-state registry; results are 24h cached.
name/address are returned only when the member state publishes them — a VAT number can be is_valid:true with name/address empty.
request_date is a compliance timestamp of the live check, useful as VIES verification evidence.
Static price ($0.005), not a dynamic quote (accepts amount 5000 = 0.005 USDC, 6 decimals).

Part of Greeneris 'eu-verify' — sibling validators (/v1/eu/eori, /v1/eu/company-check, /v1/global/lei) live on the same host as separate services. For French e-invoicing readiness (auto-computes + validates the FR VAT) use Greeneris French Invoice-Ready Check instead.
usage.guide: Validate an intra-EU VAT number against the European Commission VIES registry. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/eu/vat-check?cc=<CC>&vat=<VAT> where cc is the 2-letter member-state code (use EL for Greece, XI for Northern Ireland) and vat is the number WITHOUT the country prefix (e.g. cc=IE&vat=6388047V = GOOGLE IRELAND LIMITED). No API key — pay the x402 402 (Base USDC, $0.005) and re-request. Read data.is_valid (bool); when the member state publishes them you also get data.name and data.address, plus data.request_date as a compliance timestamp. Use for KYB / invoice compliance before trading with an EU business.
